title: Formal compositional inverse identities for logarithm and exponential
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative $\mathbf Q$-algebra and $R[[T]]$ its ring of formal power series [def-weil-formal-power-series]. Define
$$L(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}nT^n,\qquad A(T)=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1{n!}T^n.$$
For $F(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nT^n$ and $G(T)$ of constant coefficient zero, write $F\circ G=\sum_{n\ge0}f_nG(T)^n$, where each coefficient is a finite sum. Then in $R[[T]]$,
$$L\circ A=T,\qquad A\circ L=T.$$
These are identities of formal series; no topology or convergence assumption is imposed on $R$.

source.place: paragraph 3, the two formal inverse identities, separated from the analytic evaluation gap

proof.text: Write $E=1+A=\sum_{n\ge0}T^n/n!$ and use the coefficientwise derivative $D(\sum f_nT^n)=\sum(n+1)f_{n+1}T^n$. Directly from the displayed coefficients, $DE=DA=E$ and $DL=B:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nT^n$. The Cauchy product gives $(1+T)B=1$: its constant coefficient is $1$, and its coefficient in every degree $n\ge1$ is $(-1)^n+(-1)^{n-1}=0$. Also $A(0)=L(0)=0$ and $E(0)=1$. These computations use only rational arithmetic in $R$.

source.place: paragraph 3, formal inverse identities; agent-supplied coefficient proof: differentiate the defining coefficients and multiply the geometric series

proof.text: Put $H=L\circ A$. The chain rule [lem-wf-formal-substitution-chain-rule], applicable because $A(0)=0$, gives $DH=(B\circ A)E$. Substitute $A$ into $(1+T)B=1$ using the algebra homomorphism [lem-wf-formal-substitution-hom]: $(1+A)(B\circ A)=1$. Since $1+A=E$ and multiplication is commutative, $DH=1$.

source.place: paragraph 3, formal inverse identities; agent-supplied coefficient proof: differentiate L composed with A and substitute A into the geometric product

proof.text: The constant term of $H=L\circ A$ is zero: in the defining coefficientwise composition every positive power of $A$ has zero constant coefficient and $L(0)=0$. Write $H=\sum h_nT^n$. The equality $DH=1$ says $h_1=1$ and $(n+1)h_{n+1}=0$ for every $n\ge1$. Multiplication by the rational element $1/(n+1)$ gives $h_{n+1}=0$. Together with $h_0=0$, this proves $L\circ A=T$.

source.place: paragraph 3, formal inverse identities; agent-supplied coefficient proof: recover the first identity from its derivative and constant term

proof.text: Put $K=E\circ L$. The chain rule [lem-wf-formal-substitution-chain-rule], applicable because $L(0)=0$, and $DE=E$ give $DK=K B$. Hence $(1+T)DK=K$ by $(1+T)B=1$. The substitution homomorphism [lem-wf-formal-substitution-hom] fixes $1$ and preserves subtraction, so $A\circ L=(E-1)\circ L=K-1$.

source.place: paragraph 3, formal inverse identities; agent-supplied coefficient proof: differentiate E composed with L and reduce the second identity to a coefficient recurrence

proof.text: The constant coefficient of $K=E\circ L$ is $1$: only the constant term of $E$ contributes because $L(0)=0$. Write $K=\sum k_nT^n$. At degree $0$, $(1+T)DK=K$ gives $k_1=k_0=1$. At degree $n\ge1$ it gives $(n+1)k_{n+1}+nk_n=k_n$, or $(n+1)k_{n+1}=(1-n)k_n$. For $n=1$ this gives $2k_2=0$, hence $k_2=0$. Inductively, if $n\ge2$ and $k_n=0$, the recurrence gives $k_{n+1}=0$ after multiplication by $1/(n+1)$. Thus $K=1+T$, and step 4 gives $A\circ L=T$. Every composition and every coefficient calculation above is finite in each degree; the argument applies also to the zero ring and to rational algebras with nilpotents, without any topology.
